title: ProtocolSchema
description:
Every wire type, referenced once, so that `schema_for!(ProtocolSchema)`
covers the whole protocol. `docs/protocol.schema.json` is this type's
schema; the `$defs` are the protocol.

Not a message: nothing serialises a `ProtocolSchema`. Its fields are grouped
by the three tables of `30-protocol.md` — events, slots, requests — plus
the envelope and the shared types.

AssistantMessage.description: What the model said, with the provider bookkeeping the session format keeps.

content.description: Text, thinking and tool-call blocks, in order.

rawStopReason.description: The provider's own stop reason string, unmapped.

responseId.description: The provider's response id, when it gives one.

ChangedBy.description: What wrote the file an `fs.changed` reports.

oneOf.description: One of the loop's tools wrote it during a tool call.
The write was noticed at the end of the turn.

CommandInfo.description:
A slash command the loop's policy defines: an `input` match with a name
and a description (D-13), so a UI can list and complete it.

oneOf.description:
Plain text. In an assistant message this is what the model said; in a
user or tool-result message, what it reads.

textSignature.description:
Provider signature over the text, when the provider requires it to
be sent back verbatim.

oneOf.description: An image, base64-encoded.
Model reasoning, when the model exposes it.

redacted.description: True when the provider withheld the reasoning text.

oneOf.description: The model asking for a tool to run.

arguments.description: The arguments, a JSON object matching the tool's `parameters`.

id.description:
Provider-assigned call id; the tool result answers it by
`toolCallId`.

name.description: The tool's name in the loop's manifest.

thoughtSignature.description: Provider signature over the model's thinking that led to this call.

ConversationInfo.description: A conversation on disk, whether or not a loop currently runs on it (D-28).

cwd.description: The working directory it was recorded in.

id.description: The conversation id; `loop.create { session }` continues it.

name.description: The conversation's display name, if one was set.

updated.description: Unix milliseconds of the last entry.

Cost.description: Cost of a message in the provider's currency, by token class.

cacheRead.description: Cost of tokens read from the prompt cache.

cacheWrite.description: Cost of tokens written to the prompt cache.

Delta.description: A streamed fragment of an assistant message, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description: More text for the text block at `index`.

index.description: Index of the content block within the message being streamed.

oneOf.description: More reasoning for the thinking block at `index`.

index.description: Index of the content block within the message being streamed.

DslCheckParams.description:
`dsl.check` params: run the policy loader and checker on the server, where
the files live. What `pirs check` calls.

cwd.description: The directory whose policy files (with the user's global ones) to check.

DslCheckResult.description: `dsl.check` result: the merged view a loop in `cwd` would start with.

conflicts.description: Conflicts, each naming both files. Empty when the policy is clean.

files.description: The policy files found, in load order.

rendered.description:
The server's human-readable rendering of the composed policy: the
files with their intents, the merged `[settings]` and where each key
came from, and every slot's entries with their origin. Display text,
not a second schema — a client prints it, it does not parse it (D-40).

system_prompt.description:
The fully assembled system prompt, with every rewrite applied and
visible (D-21).

DslConflict.description: A composition error between two policy files.

message.description: What conflicts (a duplicate key, two replacements of one prompt, …).

Empty.description:
An empty result `{}`; the response of every request that has nothing to
return.

Envelope.description:
One line on the wire, in any direction.

Untagged: a message with `method` and `id` is a request, with `method`
and no `id` a notification, and with `id` and no `method` a response.

anyOf.description: A reply to an earlier request.

Event.description:
Every event, tagged by `method` with its `params`. Serialises as the two
members of an [`RpcNotification`]; [`Event::into_rpc`] adds the envelope.

oneOf.description: State change.
Streamed delta or complete message.
A turn ended.
A run ended; the loop is idle.
Status key changed.
Widget changed.
Notice for the user.
A file was written by the loop's tools.

FsChangedEvent.description:
`fs.changed`: one of the loop's own tools wrote a file. There is no
watcher; files changed by anything else are not reported.

path.description: The file, as the server names it; readable with `fs.read`.

name.description: The entry's name within the listed directory, for display.

path.description:
The entry's full path, as the server spells it: hand it back to
`fs.list` or `fs.read` unchanged; never parse or join it (D-31).

oneOf.description: A regular file (or a symlink to one).
A directory.

loop.description: The loop whose server reads the directory.

path.description: A directory on that server; relative paths are relative to the loop's cwd.

entries.description: The directory's entries, sorted by name.

loop.description: The loop whose server reads the file.

path.description: A file on that server, or a `ref` from an earlier by-reference payload.

FsReadResult.description:
`fs.read` result: the content inline when it is small enough, otherwise a
reference (D-11). A `ref` handed back to `fs.read` is served inline in
full, whatever its size.

anyOf.description: The file's content as UTF-8 text.
The content is above the threshold; fetch it by its `ref`.

HelloParams.description: `hello` params: the first message on every connection.

client.description: The client's name and version, free text for logs (`pirs-tui 0.1.0`).

protocol_version.description:
The server's protocol version. Same major as the client's, or the
request failed with `VERSION_REFUSED` instead.

server.description: The server's name and version, free text.

Id.description:
A JSON-RPC request id: an integer or a string, chosen by the sender and
echoed in the reply. Clients pick ids for their requests; the server picks
ids for the slot requests it sends to handlers.

InputPayload.description: `input` payload: a prompt on its way to the model.

text.description:
The text the user (or a client) sent, after any earlier `input`
handler's rewrite.

anyOf.description:
The text to hand on (unchanged, rewritten, or expanded from a slash
command).

text.description: The text the model will see.

anyOf.description: The input was consumed; nothing reaches the model and no turn starts.

loop.description: The loop whose current turn to abort (Esc). Idle loops are unaffected.

LoopAttachResult.description:
`loop.attach` result: what a client needs to render the loop and to
`subscribe` from the right point.

seq.description:
The latest `seq` in the loop's log; `subscribe { since: seq }` from
here misses nothing.

loop.description: The loop to close. Its processes are killed; its conversation stays.

model.description: Model to run; absent means the server's default.

name.description: A name for the loop and its conversation, shown in lists.

session.description:
A conversation id to continue (from `loop.list`'s `conversations`);
absent starts a new conversation.

LoopInfo.description: A running loop, as `loop.create`, `loop.list` and `loop.attach` describe it.

conversation.description: The id of the conversation (session log) this loop appends to.

cwd.description: The working directory the loop's tools and policy files are relative to.

id.description: Short random id, unique on this server for its lifetime.

model.description: The model the loop currently runs.

name.description: The name given at `loop.create`, if any.

parent.description:
The loop that created this one through a `[[tool]] loop = …` call;
absent for a top-level loop. Closing the parent closes it.

cwd.description:
When present, `conversations` in the result lists the conversations
recorded for this directory; when absent it is empty. Running loops
are listed regardless.

conversations.description:
Conversations on disk for the requested `cwd`, most recent first;
empty when no `cwd` was given.

loops.description: Every running loop on this server.

LoopMessageEvent.description:
`loop.message`: conversation traffic — streaming assistant text and
thinking as deltas, then each complete message.

role.description: The role of the message this belongs to.

seq.description: Log sequence number; absent on deltas, which are not logged.

anyOf.description: A fragment of the assistant message being streamed. Carries no `seq`.

A complete message appended to the conversation: the user's prompt as
the model saw it, the finished assistant message (including its tool
calls), or a tool result.

LoopModelParams.description: `loop.model` params: change the loop's model between turns.

spec.description: The new model and thinking level.

text.description:
The prompt text. It passes through the `input` slot before the model
sees it.

LoopReloadParams.description:
`loop.reload` params: re-read the loop's policy files now. The server
also does this by itself when one of the loop's own tools writes a policy
file (D-33).

files.description: The policy files now loaded, in load order.

LoopRunEndEvent.description:
`loop.run_end`: the loop went idle after a prompt — no more tool calls to
run and no queued prompt.

messages.description: Every message the run appended, across all its turns.

LoopSelector.description: A loop id, or "*" for every loop on the server including ones created later.

LoopState.description:
What a loop is doing. There is no third state: nothing but the model asks
the user anything, and it does so in text and then goes idle (D-37).

oneOf.description: A turn is running: the model is generating or a tool is executing.
Stopped; will do nothing until prompted.

detail.description:
One line about why, when there is something to say (`aborted`,
`error: …`, `closed`).

since.description: Unix milliseconds when the state changed.

LoopToolsParams.description: `loop.tools` params: set the loop's active tool set.

names.description: Names from the manifest; tools not listed are disabled for the loop.

LoopTurnEndEvent.description:
`loop.turn_end`: the model stopped once (a turn ends at every stop reason;
a `toolUse` stop is followed by tool results and another turn).

messages.description: The messages this turn appended, in order.

loop.description: The loop to wait for. The response arrives when it is idle.

state.description:
The loop's state when the wait ended; `idle` unless the loop was
closed meanwhile.

Manifest.description:
The loop's merged manifest: everything its policy files and built-ins
contribute that a client needs to render or complete.

status_keys.description:
Keys that `ui.status` events may carry, so a status line can be laid
out before the first event.

tools.description:
Tools the model can call, built-in and policy-defined, after
disabling and wrapping.

Message.description:
A conversation message, tagged by `role`. This is the element type of
`loop.turn_end { messages }`, `loop.run_end { messages }` and
`loop.message { message }`, and the `message` member of a session-log entry.

oneOf.description: `role: "system"`.
`role: "user"`.
`role: "assistant"`.
`role: "toolResult"`.

ModelSpec.description: Which model a loop runs, and how hard it thinks.

model.description:
The model as `provider/id` (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`,
`faux/scripted`) or a bare id the server's registry resolves.

thinking.description: Thinking level; absent means the server's default for the model.

oneOf.description: Informational.
Something to look at, e.g. a handler timed out and was skipped.
Something failed.

files.description: The policy files now loaded, in load order.

args.description: The arguments the model called it with.

result.description: The result as the model reads it (after any `tool_result` rewrite).

PromptPayload.description: `prompt` payload: the system prompt as assembled so far.

anyOf.description: Append this text to the prompt.

append.description: Text appended after the current prompt.

PromptWhen.description: When a prompt is delivered relative to the running turn.

oneOf.description:
Steer: deliver at the next opportunity inside the current turn, or
immediately when idle.
After the current turn ends (after the model's next stop).
Queue as the next input, after the run ends.

Ref.description:
A payload that travels by reference because it is above the size threshold
(64 KB by default).

The server writes the content to a file in the loop's session directory
and sends this instead. `ref` is itself a [`ServerPath`] that `fs.read`
serves, so one request fetches it; `bytes` is the content's size so a
client can decide whether to.

bytes.description: Size of the content in bytes.

ref.description: Where the content is; read it with `fs.read { loop, path: ref }`.

RegisterParams.description:
`register` params: become a handler for a slot on a loop. The server then
sends this connection a [`SlotRequest`](crate::SlotRequest) each time the
slot fires and waits up to `timeout` for the reply. A registration ends
with `unregister`, with the loop, or when the connection drops.

timeout.description:
How long the server waits for a reply, in milliseconds. Expiry counts
as "no opinion" (the slot's default outcome) plus a `ui.notify`
warning.

Request.description:
Every request a client may send, tagged by `method` with its `params`.

Serialises as `{ "method": "<name>", "params": { … } }`, the two members of
an [`RpcRequest`]; [`Request::into_rpc`] adds the envelope.

oneOf.description:
First message on every connection. Result: [`HelloResult`]. Fails with
`VERSION_REFUSED` when the majors differ.
Start a loop. Result: [`LoopInfo`].

List running loops and, for a `cwd`, its conversations. Result:
[`LoopListResult`].

Attach: get the loop, its manifest and its latest `seq`. Result:
[`LoopAttachResult`].
Close a loop and kill its processes. Result: [`Empty`].
Send a prompt. Result: [`Empty`]; the model's answer arrives as events.
Abort the current turn. Result: [`Empty`].
Block until the loop is idle. Result: [`LoopWaitResult`].

Observe events. Result: [`Empty`]; replayed events follow if `since`
was given.
Stop observing. Result: [`Empty`].
Handle a slot. Result: [`Empty`].
Stop handling a slot. Result: [`Empty`].
Emit a `ui.status` event. Result: [`Empty`].
Emit a `ui.widget` event. Result: [`Empty`].
Emit a `ui.notify` event. Result: [`Empty`].
List a directory on the loop's server. Result: [`FsListResult`].
Read a file on the loop's server. Result: [`FsReadResult`].
Set the active tool set. Result: [`Empty`].
Change the model. Result: [`Empty`].
Re-read policy files. Result: [`LoopReloadResult`].
Check policy files for a directory. Result: [`DslCheckResult`].

Role.description: A message role, as the `role` tag spells it.

oneOf.description: The system prompt.
The user.
The model.
A tool answering a tool call.

RpcError.description: The `error` member of a failed response.

RpcNotification.description:
A notification: `{ jsonrpc, method, params }` with no `id`, so no reply is
possible. Every [`Event`](crate::Event) travels as one.

params.description: The event payload, always a JSON object in this protocol.

RpcRequest.description:
A request: `{ jsonrpc, id, method, params }`. Expects exactly one
[`RpcResponse`] with the same `id`.

Client → server requests have a [`Request`](crate::Request) method; server →
handler requests have a [`Slot`](crate::Slot) as their method.

params.description: The method's parameters, always a JSON object in this protocol.

RpcResponse.description:
A response: `{ jsonrpc, id, result }` on success or `{ jsonrpc, id, error }`
on failure — never both.

id.description: The id of the request being answered.

result.description: The result, present on success. `{}` for requests without a result.

ServerPath.description:
A path on the server that runs the loop.

Every path in every message is one of these: a label the server produced
and that a client only ever hands back to the same server (`fs.list`,
`fs.read`, `loop.create { cwd }`). Clients do not parse, join, normalise or
open it — it may belong to a machine or container the client cannot see.
Accordingly this type has no filesystem operations and no conversion to
`std::path::Path`; a server converts at its own edge.

Slot.description: A handler slot: `input`, `prompt`, `tool_result`, `tool.<name>` or `on.<event>` where event is start, turn_end, run_end, tool_result or reload. Also the `method` of the request the server sends the handler.

oneOf.description: Still streaming; never appears in a complete message.
The model finished its turn.
The output token limit was reached.
The model called one or more tools; the loop runs them and continues.
The provider returned an error; see `errorMessage`.
The turn was aborted (`loop.abort`).

SubscribeParams.description:
`subscribe` params: become an observer of a loop's events. Observers are
never waited on.

events.description:
Event names to receive (`loop.message`, `fs.changed`, …); absent means
all.

since.description:
Replay sequenced events with `seq` greater than this from the session
log before live ones, across runs. Deltas are not replayed (D-06).
`0` replays everything; absent replays nothing.

SystemMessage.description: The system prompt, as recorded in the session log.

content.description: The prompt text (empty when `sections` carries it).

sections.description:
Named prompt sections; `null` removes a section set by an earlier
system message. Replaying system messages in order yields the current
prompt.

toolsAdded.description: Tool declarations added to the loadout by this message.

ThinkingLevel.description:
How much the model should think. Mirrors the server's model layer; the
server maps it to each provider's budget or effort setting.

oneOf.description: No extended thinking.
The smallest budget the provider allows.
A small budget.
A medium budget.
A large budget.
A very large budget.
The largest budget the provider allows.

ToolCallPayload.description: `tool.<name>` payload: the model called the tool.

args.description: The arguments, matching the tool's `parameters` schema.

id.description: The tool-call id, for correlating with the session log.

ToolContent.description:
Tool output content: a bare string (one text block) or a list of text and
image blocks.

anyOf.description: A string, equivalent to one text block.

ToolInfo.description:
A tool declaration: the shape the model is shown and the manifest lists.
Also the element type of a system message's `toolsAdded`.

description.description: What the tool does, as the model reads it.

name.description: The tool's name, as the model calls it.

parameters.description: JSON Schema (an object schema) for the tool's arguments.

ToolReply.description:
What a tool produced: the `tool.<name>` reply, and the `result` a
`tool_result` handler sees and returns.

details.description: Metadata for UIs, not sent to the model.

anyOf.description: The tool failed; the model reads `error` as an error result.

ToolResultMessage.description:
The result of a tool call, as the model reads it. When a `tool_result`
handler rewrote it, this is the rewritten one; the session log holds the
original beside it.

content.description: Text and image blocks the model reads.

details.description: Tool-specific metadata not sent to the model (shown by UIs).

isError.description: Whether the tool failed; the content is then the error text.

toolCallId.description: The `id` of the tool-call block being answered.

usage.description: LLM usage the tool itself incurred (e.g. a `loop` tool).

ToolResultPayload.description: `tool_result` payload: a result on its way to the model.

args.description: The arguments the model called it with.

result.description:
The result the model reads instead. The original stays in the session
log beside it.

UiNotifyEvent.description:
`ui.notify`: a one-off message for the user. Print mode shows it on
stderr; the TUI shows it as a notice.

UiNotifyParams.description: `ui.notify` params: ask the server to emit a `ui.notify` event.

text.description: The new text; empty clears the key.

UiStatusParams.description: `ui.status` params: ask the server to emit a `ui.status` event.

key.description: The status key (one of the manifest's `status_keys`, or a new one).

text.description: One line of text; empty clears the key.

lines.description: Lines to draw; empty removes the widget.

UiWidgetParams.description: `ui.widget` params: ask the server to emit a `ui.widget` event.

lines.description: Lines to draw; empty removes the widget.

cacheRead.description: Tokens read from the prompt cache.

cacheWrite.description: Tokens written to the prompt cache.

reasoning.description: Reasoning tokens, when the provider reports them separately.

totalTokens.description: Sum of input, output, cache read and cache write.

UserContent.description:
`string | Content[]`: the content of system and user messages, which the
session format allows as a bare string.

anyOf.description: A bare string, equivalent to one text block.
A list of blocks (text and images).

UserMessage.description: What the user (or a rewriting `input` handler) said.

content.description: Text, or text and image blocks.
